24bb6d01f2508e4001990348616aff2cadc34cd1.summary: Overview by Sekoia and Kudelski Security of North Korea's (DPRK) cyber organisation. It covers the state bodies with offensive cyber mandates (GRIB, formerly RGB; NIA, formerly MSS; the KWP), DPRK-nexus clusters tracked as APTs (including Lazarus sub-clusters, Kimsuky, Andariel, Moonstone Sleet, Reaper), the fake IT worker programme, and revenue from cryptocurrency theft and laundering, including through Cambodia. The report stresses frequent reorganisation and differing vendor naming.

243c3c5089789e3b641c19f5ff997c631beacc9f.summary: Malware analysis of a Linux crypto-miner found on a customer endpoint. The authors conclude the Go binary is a component of the Sysrv botnet. They describe a shell loader that disables the firewall and uses SSH keys to spread, cron-based persistence, a config file that points to a remote server, built-in exploits against web applications, and hardcoded username/password lists for brute-forcing logins. Published 2024-04-14.

249c26fd265ef866cc2990bcbbac23d2e8eb104e.summary: HTC Global Services, a managed service provider, confirmed a cybersecurity incident after the ALPHV (BlackCat) ransomware gang listed it on its leak site with screenshots of allegedly stolen data. Researcher Kevin Beaumont believes initial access came through a vulnerable Citrix Netscaler device (Citrix Bleed) at the CareTech business unit. The report also gives background on ALPHV and its recent victims.
